measured_execution_comparison.measurement_method: Three fresh local CLI subprocess samples per invoked route variant; wall time and child CPU from the local macOS process, plus UTF-8 stdin/stdout bytes. No network or external runner.

default_full_task.outcome: NO_TOOL_RUN; required association outputs unavailable by default

light_baseline.route_profile: job interval summary only; same underlying run snapshot, narrower output contract

redundant_counterfactual.task_outcome: COMPLETE; no additional required job-interval fact beyond attribution output; standalone timeline adds unused per-step detail for this frozen task
redundant_counterfactual.reason_not_selected: With both IDs allowlisted, the planner selected the attribution tool alone for this job-level task; the extra timeline invocation was measured only as a redundant counterfactual.

result_and_cost_interpretation: The default-off route correctly did not call either experimental tool and left this specialist task incomplete.
The explicitly selected light timeline route completed only the narrower interval task; it did not bind the plan, target list or artifact receipt.
The attribution tool alone met the frozen job-level attribution contract. Allowlisting both still selected only attribution.

Manually running timeline plus attribution as a counterfactual reproduced the same required interval facts and added unnecessary step details and a second process. In these three local samples its median wall/CPU time and I/O bytes are reported above; this is task-local evidence, not a general performance claim.
limits: One real PR #264 run fixture; caller-supplied and unauthenticated inputs.
No cash, hosted-runner billing, token cost, long-run reliability or general performance claim.
Observed 1,998 seconds are recorded workflow job intervals, not the experiment process time and not billable minutes.
Router proposals do not invoke the tool or grant authority. The experiment explicitly allowlisted and manually executed only offline read-only CLIs.
